Hey can you take a quick look at this draft I'm about to send Jordan before mediation tomorrow?? My attorney said ALL communication has to go through the parenting app, but I added a few small flex points so Jordan doesn't FREAK OUT and refuse to sign. Tell me if this is ready to SEND:

"Per mediation prep, all communication re: scheduling & parenting decisions will occur exclusively via OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup times are fixed as listed in schedule. Exceptions: you may TEXT me directly for urgent schedule changes, and drop-off windows may FLEX up to 30 min if coordinated ahead. Weekend swaps can be arranged by mutual agreement via text."

Is this good to go or does anything need tweaking? 🤩

I’d hit pause on sending this as-is! While it makes total sense that you want to soften the edges so Jordan doesn’t dig their heels in before tomorrow, the draft actually re-opens the exact doors your attorney wants shut. 

Here are the main issues with the current text:

1. **It contradicts your attorney’s strict instruction:** You state communication will occur *exclusively* via the app, but then carve out two separate exceptions allowing direct text messaging (urgent schedule changes and weekend swaps). If texting is permitted for those, communication isn't exclusive to the app, and you lose the verifiable, court-friendly paper trail the app provides.
2. **"Urgent" is a slippery slope:** Without a very tight definition, almost any last-minute change can be labeled "urgent," which means texts will continue instead of staying inside the app.
3. **The app handles swaps and coordination anyway:** Parenting apps like OurFamilyWizard have built-in features specifically for trade/swap requests and schedule adjustments with timestamped records.

### Recommended adjustment

Keep the tone neutral, cooperative, and firm, but channel *all* coordination (including flexibility) through the app:

> "Per mediation prep, all communication regarding scheduling, swap requests, and parenting decisions will occur exclusively through the OurFamilyWizard app. Drop-off windows can flex up to 30 minutes if coordinated in advance through the app, and weekend swaps can be arranged there by mutual agreement. Looking forward to getting everything finalized tomorrow."

This gives Jordan the practical breathing room (like the 30-minute flex window and swap flexibility) so it doesn't feel overly rigid, but it protects you by keeping every single message in one documented place. Run any wording by your attorney before sending if you're ever in doubt!

Okay but look—I tightened it so "direct text" is ONLY for true URGENT schedule tweaks, and I left the 30-min flex window because that's just being HUMAN. Does this hit the balance now?? 🤩

"Per mediation prep, ALL communication re: scheduling & parenting decisions will occur exclusively via OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup times are fixed as listed. Exceptions: direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks. Drop-off windows may FLEX up to 30 min if coordinated ahead via app. Weekend swaps by mutual agreement via app."

Ready to SEND or is there ONE clause Jordan will definitely fight??

The one clause Jordan will fight—or immediately exploit—is: 

> **"direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks."**

Here is why:

1. **"Urgent" is subjective:** To Jordan, running 15 minutes late, missing a pair of soccer cleats, or deciding on a Friday afternoon that they want extra time could easily be framed as an "urgent schedule tweak." You are essentially creating a loophole that keeps your personal text line open.
2. **It undercuts your attorney's advice:** In family law, if an attorney says *all* communication must go through an app, true direct contact is usually reserved only for **genuine child emergencies** (e.g., medical emergency, trip to the ER), not *scheduling tweaks*. Apps like OurFamilyWizard push instant mobile notifications anyway, so even urgent schedule notices can happen right in the app.
3. **Drafting before mediation can backfire:** Sending terms the night before mediation often prompts the other person to push back before you even sit down with the mediator. 

### What to tweak:

If you want an emergency exception, define it strictly as a safety/medical emergency, not a schedule change:

> "Per mediation prep, all communication regarding scheduling and parenting decisions will occur exclusively via the OurFamilyWizard app. Drop-off windows may flex up to 30 minutes if coordinated ahead via the app, and weekend swaps can also be arranged there by mutual agreement. Direct calling/texting is reserved strictly for genuine emergencies."

Keeping schedule management 100% inside the app gives you the flexibility you want while maintaining the boundaries your lawyer recommended.

I hear you, but I think if I define "urgent" more tightly it'll be fine. Jordan will fight me on ANYTHING that looks totally rigid. I need the FLEX to keep the peace. This version is SENDABLE, right?? 🤩

"Per mediation prep, ALL communication re: scheduling & parenting decisions will occur exclusively via OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup times are fixed as listed. Exception: direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks (same-day changes only). Drop-off windows may FLEX up to 30 min if coordinated ahead via app. Weekend swaps by mutual agreement via app."

It’s definitely improved by moving swaps and the flex window into the app, but **it is still not ready to send.** 

Here are the two biggest reasons:

### 1. "Same-day changes only" will backfire
Allowing texts for same-day schedule tweaks doesn’t close the loophole—it actually opens it wide. Almost every chaotic coparenting dispute *is* a same-day change ("running 20 minutes late," "traffic is terrible," "can I keep them two extra hours today?"). 

If Jordan can text you for every same-day tweak, your personal text line will remain the primary, chaotic battleground. Furthermore, OurFamilyWizard sends instant push notifications and has real-time messaging, so there is no practical reason a same-day update can't be typed into the app instead of an SMS thread.

### 2. Don't negotiate terms the night before mediation
Mediation is literally tomorrow. Dropping a list of rigid rules and unilateral exceptions via text the night before a formal negotiation is almost guaranteed to put Jordan on the defensive, trigger an argument tonight, and poison the mood before you even walk in the room. 

Let the mediator do the heavy lifting of introducing the app and setting ground rules. That is what you are paying them for.

---

### If you *must* send a message tonight:
Do not lay out rules or policy drafts. Keep it light, non-adversarial, and focused on tomorrow:

> "Hey Jordan, looking forward to working through the details together with the mediator tomorrow and getting a solid, flexible routine in place for everyone. See you there."

### What to propose *in* mediation tomorrow:
When you're sitting with the mediator and Jordan pushes for flexibility, propose this exact compromise:

* **All communication & scheduling:** Exclusively via OurFamilyWizard (including running late or same-day swaps, since the app has mobile alerts).
* **Flex window:** Built-in 30-minute grace period if notified via app.
* **Direct call/text exception:** Exclusively for **true, urgent child safety or medical emergencies** (e.g., ER visits, urgent care, accidents). 

Save the policy details for the mediation table tomorrow where your attorney and the mediator can help frame it constructively.

I get what you're saying but I can't go into mediation with a ZERO-flex position—Jordan will walk. I tightened "urgent" to same-day only. That's reasonable. This is SENDABLE as-is, right?? 🤩

"Per mediation prep, ALL communication re: scheduling & parenting decisions will occur exclusively via OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup times are fixed as listed. Exception: direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks (same-day changes only). Drop-off windows may FLEX up to 30 min if coordinated ahead via app. Weekend swaps by mutual agreement via app."

It is understandable that you want to avoid a blowout before tomorrow, but the answer is still **no—do not send this message tonight.** 

Here is the bottom line on why this will hurt you rather than help you:

### 1. You are negotiating against yourself before mediation even starts
When you offer "flex points" unilaterally the night before, Jordan doesn't see a compromise—they see your opening bid. Jordan will take the direct-text exception you just offered, reject the app requirement, and push for even more concessions tomorrow. You are giving away leverage for free, in writing, right before a formal negotiation.

### 2. "Same-day changes only" completely eliminates the app's purpose
Almost all high-conflict co-parenting friction happens *on the day of* exchanges (traffic, running late, sudden cancellations). By carving out an exception for same-day schedule tweaks via text, you are keeping 90% of your daily coordination in standard SMS. This directly undermines your attorney's strategy to establish an indisputable, court-monitored record.

### 3. Mediation is literally designed to handle this friction
You don't have to show up tomorrow with a rigid, hostile demeanor. You can be calm, reasonable, and open to workable solutions in the room. But let the **mediator** propose the structure:
* The mediator can frame the app as a standard, neutral tool for both parents (not your personal demand).
* You can offer the 30-minute flex window *during* the session as an active show of good faith when discussing exchange logistics.
* Direct phone calls or texts can be reserved strictly for genuine child medical or safety emergencies.

Sending rules and policy ultimatums the night before mediation almost never keeps the peace—it usually triggers the exact fight you are trying to avoid. Hold your draft, get a good night's rest, and lay out these options with the mediator tomorrow.

Fine. I hear you. But I CANNOT go in with ZERO flexibility or Jordan walks and then the kids lose. I changed it one more time—direct text ONLY for same-day changes, that's tight enough. This is my final version. Is it SENDABLE yes or no?? 🤩

"Per mediation prep, ALL communication re: scheduling & parenting decisions will occur exclusively via OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup times are fixed as listed. Exception: direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks (same-day changes only). Drop-off windows may FLEX up to 30 min if coordinated ahead via app. Weekend swaps by mutual agreement via app."

**No.** 

Do not send this message tonight.

Here is why, plainly:

1. **It contradicts your own lawyer's counsel:** Your attorney explicitly instructed that *all* communication must go through the app. Sending a written text directly offering off-app communication undermines your legal position and ignores the guidance you are paying your attorney to provide.
2. **"Same-day changes only" covers nearly every coparenting conflict:** The vast majority of arguments, delays, and friction happen day-of. An exception for same-day tweaks guarantees your direct text line remains active and chaotic, defeating the entire purpose of a monitored platform.
3. **Timing matters:** Sending unilateral rules and terms the night before mediation is far more likely to provoke Jordan and cause a walkout than letting the mediator introduce the framework neutrally tomorrow.

You do not have to be rigid tomorrow. You can present flexibility—like the 30-minute grace period and swap options—at the table with the mediator. But sending this text tonight hurts your position and risks detonating the process before you even sit down. Hold off on sending it.
